body:
### What are you really trying to do?
Make use of JSONTypeConverter.to_typed_value

I wrote a class that's inheriting `temporalio.converter.JSONTypeConverter` and overrides `to_typed_value` to customize its behavior.

<!-- 
Tell us at a high level what you're doing, to avoid XY problem (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XY_problem) 
-->


### Describe the bug
The type the method returns is `Any | None | _JSONTypeConverterUnhandled`. The method is public and can be imported, but `_JSONTypeConverterUnhandled` is not. So I don't have a good way to type hint the return type of my method unless I import an underscore prefixed name, which triggers linters and can also be changed by you as an implementation detail as it's not part of the API.
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

<!-- If applicable, add screenshots or code blocks to help explain your problem. You can also use [Loom](http://loom.com/) to do short, free video bug reports. -->

comments.body: Can you elaborate on the use case? I just want to understand the purpose of subclassing it so we understand the actual reason for the need.

We have a custom converter, for example so temporal can handle custom types we have across our codebase. Technically it's not limited to subclassing. Anytime I want to use `to_typed_value`, and the function where I'm calling it doesn't handle the result itself but returns it, I'm going to run into this issue.

title: [Bug] Unexposed return type of public method
